P1.evidence: Nothing was read back from the setter, but the substitute question was the most useful opening in the batch: 'How was that conversation for you?' followed by 'What do you mean by cryptic?' surfaced within thirty seconds that the prospect had asked the setter about cost and schedule and been given no answer. The rep then squandered it by deflecting rather than correcting. Frame was two-part plus alignment; agreement checked with 'All righty?' and answered 'Sure'; open question ran verbatim.

P2.evidence: The strongest baseline in the batch on the factual half. Age, height and weight were all asked directly and in sequence — the only call here where that happens. Training history was properly interrogated, including the best follow-up on the call: told the conditioning work had been programmed but skipped, the rep asked 'Oh Fred, why? What's going on?' Results were checked with 'Have you lost any weight recently, or have you been putting on weight?' and diet was covered thoroughly, extending into fasting and daily steps. The gap is health. No health-conditions question was asked, and when the prospect volunteered blood-work findings of a below-average metabolic rate and high cortisol, the rep did not follow up on either — which matters, because a fat-loss goal on top of an endocrine finding is precisely where the programme's fasting protocol would conflict with his nutritionist's advice. No injuries question, no sleep, no energy.

P3.evidence: The phase barely ran. The physique question was asked — 'What kind of physique are you going for?' — and answered 'I never really thought about it', and the rep let it go rather than helping him build one. From there nothing: no bridge, no 'what does that do for you', nobody else's stake, nothing on identity or longevity. The only goal established in fifteen minutes was a number, ten kilos, and a suit that no longer fits across the shoulders. With no WHY established, the price at 00:12:23 had nothing to land against, which is the mechanical reason the call ended where it did.

P4.evidence: Past attempts were mapped well — years of programme-hopping, two months with a current personal trainer, and the specific failure of bulking up on every rep scheme he tried. What happened was drawn out clearly, including the admission that he skipped the conditioning half most weeks. The gap was named by the prospect in his own words: 'the thing that would help would be to build a kettlebell routine that works for my life and that has the validation that, okay, that's enough... you don't need to supplement it with anything.' The rep heard it and did not build on it. 'Why do you feel it didn't stick' was reduced to a single light exchange answered 'time-wise', and the root-cause reframe never ran.

P5.evidence: Never ran in any form. No two-year projection, no settling question, no line in the sand.

P6.evidence: The belief question was never asked. The all-in concept was central to the call but was asserted rather than elicited — 'I want to make sure you're ready' and 'I want to make sure that if we go through that, [it's] something firstly that you want, and secondly that you're all in on' — with the rep answering it on the prospect's behalf instead of putting the question to him. P6c is a clean hit and the most script-faithful moment in this batch: the gate says move forward only on a clear yes, there was no clear yes, and the rep did not move forward.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted. The price was named and the offer was then deliberately withdrawn, so the payment and onboarding phase was never reachable. Marked not applicable rather than miss so the phase drops out of the denominator.

objection_plays.detail: The trigger was unmistakable — 'Oh wow. Okay.' and later 'definitely wasn't expecting the cost' — and not one move ran. No isolation, no HOW-not-SHOULD reframe, no financial picture. Recorded as a miss, but as a deliberate non-play rather than an oversight: the rep had already begun withdrawing the offer in the same breath as naming the price, and chose disqualification over working the objection. That is a defensible judgement given the prospect had described himself as exploring rather than buying, and it is the correct read of the script's own instruction not to proceed without a yes. Worth separating in any rollup from the calls where OC simply was not run.

Script gap. The prospect's central objection was trust in the category itself — 'they always have a hidden agenda or another motive and to book more courses or to try and sell you something else' — and there is no scripted play for a prospect who distrusts coaches on principle. The rep improvised reasonably by describing the structure of the business: one coach, no junior coaches, an active client cap of 150. He then answered it far more powerfully by conduct, declining to sell and sending the prospect back to free material. Recorded as partial because the improvisation was sound but unrepeatable; this objection is common enough in a market full of upsell-driven coaching that it deserves a written play.

notes: The cleanest disqualification in the batch and genuinely good factual discovery — the only call where age, height and weight were all asked — but P3 and P5 never ran, so there was no reason built before the number was said, and the price landed as a bare figure. The judgement to walk away rather than discount is worth reinforcing. Two things to fix: when a prospect volunteers blood work showing high cortisol and a suppressed metabolic rate, follow it, because the programme's fasting protocol directly contradicts what his nutritionist has told him; and never describe the price as tailored or dependent on the individual when it is a fixed figure.
